The village is full of people this map doesn't track. Enemies appear only once SABER confirms them; "movement" calls stay off the map until SABER sees weapons, or calls them civilians (a dashed ring for a minute and a half). Any heat the gunner sees that isn't on your map is unknown. Tap a callout to find it. Talk the gunner on: grid, nearest landmark, compass direction, then the target. The gunner sees only heat. This map doesn't know what the gunner has already killed, so ask.

Pylon Turn · how to play

How to play

The idea

You fly the sensor and guns of an AC-130 orbiting a village at night. Everyone down there is heat. The gunner can shoot but can't tell friend from enemy; the radio operator knows who's who but can't shoot. Keep the ground team alive until their helicopter lifts off.

Playing as a crew

Each code is a different village, objective, route and enemy plan. No network needed: both devices pick the same code and pace, then press Start together, or both press Next full minute (easiest on phones). The mission plays out identically on both screens; if units drift apart, the radio operator can nudge the clock a second either way.

    Rules of engagement

    What this prototype tests

    Only the core question: is talking a gunner onto targets tense and fun? Loaders are automated (the reload timers are where human loaders will go), and there's no plane interior yet.
